label: Subtract fixed-point numbers
summary: The first fixed-point number minus the second.
details: Vanilla uses it in the tax collector texts to show the difference between a value breakdown's value and the value change for the current collector, printed with a sign. A tournament tooltip also uses it on an activity variable.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.values: a fixed-point number, such as a value breakdown's value

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The number that is taken away.

label: Subtract 2D vectors
summary: The first 2D vector (for example a position) minus the second, giving a new 2D vector.
details: Vanilla's ruler designer window uses it to place a widget at a colour picker's position minus (8, 8).

label: Subtract 3D vectors
summary: Going by its name, the first 3D vector minus the second.
details: The game's files never use it, so only the name and the return type support this.

label: Subtract 4D vectors
summary: Going by its name, the first 4D vector minus the second.
details: The game's files never use it, so only the name and the return type support this.

label: Subtract decimals
summary: Going by its name, the first decimal number minus the second.
details: The game's files never use it, so only the name and the return type support this.

label: Subtract whole numbers
summary: The first whole number minus the second.
details: Vanilla's legitimacy texts use it to get the highest legitimacy level number (the count of levels minus 1), and to show how many levels a vassal's expectation is above the player's current level.

label: Subtract unsigned numbers
summary: Going by its name, the first non-negative whole number minus the second.
details: The game's files never use it, so only the name and the return type support this. 'uint32' is a whole number that cannot be negative.

label: Target army
summary: The army a game text names as the target, such as the one a unit follows.
details: Vanilla's army view uses it in "Attach to follow ..." and "Detach from following ...".

label: Target building
summary: The building something changes into, in a game text.
details: Vanilla's one use: "[building] is downgraded to [target building]".

label: Target character
summary: The target character of an effect text.
details: Vanilla's effect texts take its short name and check whether it is the local player, to write 'are' for the player and 'is' for anyone else (for example, who becomes the new father).

label: Second target
summary: A second target character, in texts that name two.
details: Vanilla uses it in over 200 lines after TARGET_CHARACTER, for example an interaction between [target] and [target 2], or a hostage's warden and home court.

label: Target culture
summary: The culture a game text names as the target, such as one a scheme is started against.
details: Vanilla uses it in almost 90 lines, for example "Starts a ... scheme against [culture]".

label: Target faith
summary: The faith a text or tooltip is about as its target, going by the name and the return type.
details: Nothing in the game's files uses it.

label: Second target faith
summary: A second faith a text can name as a target, going by the name and the return type.
details: Nothing in the game's files uses it. TARGET_FAITH is the first one.

label: New holding type
summary: The kind of holding a holding changes into, in a game text.
details: Vanilla's one use: the holding "changes from [HOLDING_TYPE] to [TARGET_HOLDING_TYPE]".

label: Previous law
summary: The law a change starts from, in texts that change a law.
details: Vanilla's effect texts write "change the ... law from [TARGET_LAW] to [LAW]", so here it is the law being replaced.

label: Target title
summary: The title a game text names as the target, such as one a scheme is started against.
details: Vanilla uses it in over 150 lines, for example "Starts a ... scheme against [title]".

label: Task contract
summary: The task contract (a job a local ruler puts out, which an adventurer can take on) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it to accept a contract or to say one is invalidated, naming its type.

label: Task contract type
summary: The kind of task contract a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it to name a contract type, for example when a contract of that type is created.

label: Tax slot type
summary: A type of tax slot that a text or window is about, going by the name and the return type.
details: Nothing in the game's files uses it.

label: Tenet
summary: The faith tenet a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it for a core tenet a faith gains, named for the faith's main rite.

label: This scope
summary: The thing a text or script is currently about, which the game describes as 'Script Scope'.
details: Vanilla texts reach into it for parts, such as the character ('THIS.Char') or title ('THIS.Title') that the text is about, and sometimes print it directly.

label: Title
summary: The title a text or tooltip is about.
details: Vanilla uses it to get the holder and the adjective of a title in effect texts, and to check whether it is shown in the title view for a coat of arms tooltip.

label: Second title
summary: A second title in a text that names two.
details: Vanilla uses it in the holding view's warnings about moving a capital: some buildings in [TITLE_2] may become inactive.

label: Doctrine parameter
summary: The value of a doctrine parameter that a doctrine's text describes.
details: Vanilla uses it in doctrine parameter texts and reads it as a whole number, turned into a hostility level name ("are considered [level] instead of ...").

label: Trait
summary: The trait a text is about, going by the name and the return type.
details: The only vanilla lines found are two trigger texts that write '$TRAIT|V$' (a text placeholder), which may not be this function. Nothing else uses it.

label: Second trait
summary: A second trait in a text that names two.
details: Vanilla uses it after TRAIT, for example as the opposite trait that stops a trait from being added, or in the opinion reason "[trait] vs. [trait 2]".

label: Trait group
summary: The trait group a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in opinion reasons ("Also [group]") and in the note that a character already has a trait of the group.

label: Second trait group
summary: A second trait group in a text that names two.
details: Vanilla's one use is the opinion reason "Opinion of [group 2]", about an opposite trait group.

label: Trait level track
summary: A trait level track that a text is about, going by the name and the return type.
details: Nothing in the game's files uses it.

label: Trait level track entry
summary: One entry of a trait level track, going by the name and the return type.
details: Nothing in the game's files uses it.

label: Travel plan
summary: The travel plan (a character's journey) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's effect texts use it, for example when it is delayed or gains a modifier.

label: Travel companion
summary: A companion on a travel plan that a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's travel planner uses it to say where and when the companion joined, or which travel option made them join.

label: Triggered legend seed
summary: A legend seed a character qualifies for, in condition texts.
details: Vanilla uses it in "Qualifies for the ... legend seed" and its negation, named for the character.

label: Tutorial
summary: The tutorial a game text is about.
details: Vanilla's one use shows the name of the step when the game is paused by the tutorial.

label: Tenet pickable in rite
summary: Whether the tenet can be picked while the head of the faith is editing the faith's main rite.
details: It is false only when the rite window is editing the main rite, the faith uses tenet popularity, and the tenet is neither already part of the rite nor very popular. The rite creation window uses it to enable or grey out tenet entries.

label: Tenet popularity neutral
summary: Whether the tenet's popularity within the given faith is at the neutral level.
details: The game's own description says 'very popular', which looks like a copy mistake; the macro asks the scripted GUI 'tenet_popularity_gui_neutral', so neutral is what it checks. The faith view texts name it together with the other popularity tiers.

fields.name: Faith
fields.text: The faith in which the tenet's popularity is judged.

label: Tenet popularity popular
summary: Whether the tenet's popularity within the given faith is at the popular level.
details: The game's own description says 'very popular', which looks like a copy mistake; the macro asks the scripted GUI 'tenet_popularity_gui_popular', so popular is what it checks. The faith view texts name it together with the other popularity tiers.

fields.name: Faith
fields.text: The faith in which the tenet's popularity is judged.

label: Tenet popularity unpopular
summary: Whether the tenet's popularity within the given faith is at the unpopular level.
details: The game's own description says 'very popular', which looks like a copy mistake; the macro asks the scripted GUI 'tenet_popularity_gui_unpopular', so unpopular is what it checks. The faith view texts name it together with the other popularity tiers.

fields.name: Faith
fields.text: The faith in which the tenet's popularity is judged.

label: Tenet very popular
summary: Whether the tenet is very popular within the given faith.
details: Vanilla's faith view texts use it, together with the other popularity tiers, to pick the tier name and the icon shown for a tenet.

fields.name: Faith
fields.text: The faith in which the tenet's popularity is judged.

label: Format texture size
summary: Going by its name, turns a texture size into text.
details: It belongs to the game's internal GUI tools and is never used in the game's files.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The size to turn into text.

label: Format texture kilobytes
summary: Going by its name, turns a size in kilobytes into text.
details: It belongs to the game's internal GUI tools and is never used in the game's files.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The size to turn into text.

label: Tick day
summary: Going by its name, advances the game by one day; it returns nothing.
details: The game's files never use it, so this rests on the name only.

label: Colour as text format
summary: Turns a colour into the form the text system needs for a '#color:{...}' tag.
details: Vanilla uses it in the my-realm window, where the vassal opinion's tint is turned into a colour for the opinion number text.

label: Toggle vassal details
summary: Opens or closes the detail view of an administrative vassal's title in the government administration window.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks, with the title as its argument. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The title whose detail view is toggled.

label: Toggle army details
summary: Going by its name, opens or closes the detail view of an administrative army.
details: The game's files never use it, so this rests on the name and its sibling ToggleAdminVassalDetailView.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: What to show the detail view of.

label: Toggle encyclopedia
summary: Opens the encyclopedia, or closes it if it is open.
details: Vanilla attaches it to buttons in the main menu and the HUD. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle interaction menu
summary: Opens or closes the character interaction menu for a character, going by its name with a filter.
details: Vanilla calls it from buttons with the character and a filter name such as 'accolade', 'admin_governor' or 'celestial_ministry'. Going by the name, the filter limits which interactions are listed.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the menu is about.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The filter that picks which interactions appear.

label: Toggle funeral selection
summary: Shows or hides the 'deceased to honor' selection widget of the funeral activity.
details: It flips the GUI variable 'activity_funeral_deceased_selection'. The funeral selection button uses it on click.

label: Toggle game view
summary: Opens or closes one of the game's main views (windows) by its name.
details: Vanilla's HUD buttons use it with names such as 'outliner', 'government_administration' and 'hud_ruler_objective'. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle game view for an object
summary: Opens or closes a main view that is about one object, such as the player's court or council.
details: Vanilla's HUD buttons call it with a view name ('military', 'council_window', 'court_window') and the player's ID. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: The ID of the object the view shows.

label: Toggle hireable ruler details
summary: Going by its name, opens or closes the detail view of a hireable ruler.
details: The game's files never use it, so this rests on the name only.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The ruler whose detail view is toggled.

label: Toggle dead portrait age limit
summary: Going by its name, switches the dynasty tree's age limit for portraits of dead characters on or off.
details: Vanilla uses it once, from a click in the dynasty tree window. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle map editor map mode
summary: Going by its name, switches the map editor's use of the game's map mode on or off.
details: Vanilla uses it once, from a click in the map editor's map mode selector. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle map mode
summary: Switches a map mode (a coloured view of the map) on or off by its name.
details: Vanilla's HUD uses it with the name 'mandala'. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The name of the map mode.

label: Toggle mercenary details
summary: Opens or closes the detail view of a mercenary company in the military window.
details: Vanilla calls it from clicks, with the company as its argument. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle message settings
summary: Opens or closes the message settings, going by its name and its use on HUD buttons.
details: It returns nothing.

label: Toggle music player
summary: Opens or closes the music player.
details: Vanilla uses it on a HUD button and inside the music player view itself. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle coat of arms click
summary: Going by its name and its one use, switches what a click on a title's coat of arms does in the find-title window.
details: Vanilla passes the title's ID. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle barter map icons
summary: Going by its name, switches the detailed barter icons on the map on or off.
details: Vanilla uses it once, from a button in the map modes. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle raid map icons
summary: Going by its name, switches the detailed raid icons on the map on or off.
details: Vanilla uses it once, from a button in the map modes. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle epidemic map graphics
summary: Going by its name, switches the epidemic graphics on the map on or off.
details: Vanilla uses it once, from a button in the map modes. It returns nothing.

label: Toggle legend map graphics
summary: Going by its name, switches the legend graphics on the map on or off.
details: Vanilla uses it once, from a button in the map modes. It returns nothing.

label: Trim end of text
summary: Going by its name, the given text with its end trimmed, probably of spaces and line breaks.
details: Its one use, in the engine's script runner inspector, shows a script's result through it. What exactly is trimmed is not documented.

label: Trim chosen characters from end
summary: Going by its name, the text with the given characters removed from its end.
details: The game's files never use it, so this rests on the name only.

label: Trim start of text
summary: Going by its name, the text trimmed at its start (probably removing whitespace).
details: The game's files never use it, so this rests on the name only.

label: Trim chosen characters from start
summary: Going by its name, the text with the given characters removed from its start.
details: The game's files never use it, so this rests on the name only.

label: Start ruler designer
summary: Going by its name, tries to start the ruler designer for a character.
details: Vanilla's multiplayer setup buttons call it with the character and one of 'noble_family', 'landless_adventurer' or 'default'. What the second value changes is not documented. It returns nothing.

fields.name: Arg0
fields.text: The character the designer is started for.

fields.name: Arg1
fields.text: A name picking a kind of start.

label: Unsigned number as text
summary: Going by its name, turns a non-negative whole number into text.
details: The game's files never use it.

label: Long unsigned number as text
summary: Going by its name, turns a large non-negative whole number into text.
details: The game's files never use it.

label: Short unsigned number as text
summary: Going by its name, turns a small non-negative whole number into text.
details: The game's files never use it.

label: Unfocus widget
summary: Takes the keyboard focus away from a widget.
details: It returns nothing. The game's files do not use it; the game's own description is only 'Unfocus widget'.

label: Update ruler objective advice
summary: Going by its name, a command that refreshes the advice shown for the player ruler's objective.
details: Vanilla's ruler objective HUD sends it as a command when clicked and reads its description for the tooltip.

label: Uses default portrait
summary: Whether the character is shown with the default character view portrait.
details: It is false for a saint in a faith with abrahamic hostility, and for a landed ruler under a herder government; those get a different portrait variant. Vanilla's shared portrait GUI uses it as a visibility condition.

label: Uses timer locking
summary: Going by its name, whether the game locks its timer, returned as yes or no.
details: The game's files never use it, and the game documents nothing more.

label: Contract obligation level
summary: An obligation level of a vassal contract that a text or window is about, going by the name and the return type.
details: Nothing in the game's files uses it.

label: Vassal contract type
summary: A type of vassal contract that a text or window is about, going by the name and the return type.
details: Nothing in the game's files uses it. The return type is called SubjectContractType.

label: Vassal stance
summary: The vassal stance (a setting every vassal has that shapes their opinion of the liege and which heir they prefer) a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it with its icon and name in interaction texts: "will have the ... vassal stance".

label: War
summary: The war a game text is about.
details: Vanilla uses it in about 100 lines, for example to name the war and its attacker when it ends.

label: Watch windows enabled
summary: Going by its name, whether the debug watch windows are turned on.
details: Vanilla's debug watch window uses it as its visibility condition.

label: Weeks per year
summary: The number of weeks in a year.
details: A whole number. The game's files do not use it.

label: Why day can't advance
summary: Going by its name, a text giving the reason the game cannot advance a day.
details: The game's files never use it, so this rests on the name only.

label: Zoom level above
summary: Whether the map's current zoom level is greater than the given one.
details: It compares the current zoom level with the number you give. The game's files do not use this one; its siblings do.

fields.name: ZoomLevel
fields.text: The zoom level to compare with.
fields.values: a whole number, e.g. a game define

label: Zoom level at least
summary: Whether the map's current zoom level is greater than or equal to the given one.
details: Vanilla's map icon layer uses it with a game define to decide when a raid or barter icon changes between its simple and detailed look.

fields.name: ZoomLevel
fields.text: The zoom level to compare with.

label: Zoom level below
summary: Whether the map's current zoom level is less than the given one.
details: Vanilla's map icon layer uses it with a game define to decide when a raid or barter icon is shown in its simple form.

fields.name: ZoomLevel
fields.text: The zoom level to compare with.

label: Zoom level at most
summary: Whether the map's current zoom level is less than or equal to the given one.
details: The game's files do not use this one; its siblings do.

fields.name: ZoomLevel
fields.text: The zoom level to compare with.

label: Add 'es' for third person
summary: Gives 'es' for a verb about someone else, and nothing when the character is the local player.
details: The macro picks '' for the local player and 'es' otherwise, so one sentence works for both 'you' and another person.

fields.name: CHARACTER
fields.text: The character the sentence is about.

label: Add 's' for third person
summary: Gives 's' for a verb about someone else, and nothing when the character is the local player.
details: The macro picks '' for the local player and 's' otherwise. Vanilla's effect texts use it, as in 'transfer[_s(...)]'.

fields.name: CHARACTER
fields.text: The character the sentence is about.

label: Abandon celibacy
summary: The game concept Abandon Celibacy: a decision that lets a character drop the Celibate trait whenever they choose.
details: In a text, `[abandon_celibacy|E]` shows the words "Abandon Celibacy" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it next to `[embrace_celibacy|E]` in effect texts that unlock both decisions.

label: Abandon celibacy
summary: Another name of the game concept Abandon Celibacy: a decision that lets a character drop the Celibate trait whenever they choose.
details: In a text, `[abandon_celibacy_decision|E]` shows the words "Abandon Celibacy Decision" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text uses this name; vanilla writes `[abandon_celibacy|E]`.

label: Abandon hook interaction
summary: The game concept Abandon Hook Interaction: a character interaction that gives up a hook you hold on someone, and you lose stress in return.
details: In a text, `[abandon_hook_interaction|E]` shows "Abandon Hook Interaction" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in trait and struggle texts that unlock the interaction.

label: Absolute crown authority
summary: Another name of the game concept Absolute Crown Authority: the highest level of crown authority (the law for how much power a ruler has over their vassals).
details: In a text, `[absolute|E]` shows the word "Absolute" linked to the concept's explanation. At this level vassals have -30 opinion of their liege, the ruler can pick a designated heir for a prestige cost, and vassals cannot declare war at all, not even on foreign rulers. Vanilla uses it when listing the crown authority levels.

label: Absolute control
summary: The game concept Absolute Control: a special state of county control (how firmly the holder controls the county), unlocked by a perk.
details: In a text, `[absolute_control|E]` shows "Absolute Control" linked to the concept's explanation. With the perk, a county at 100 control counts as absolute control and gives extra taxes and levies. Vanilla uses it in the effect text that enables it and in the tax and levy bonus lines of holdings.

label: Absolute control
summary: A short name of the game concept Absolute Control: a special state of county control, unlocked by a perk, that gives extra taxes and levies at 100 control.
details: In a text, `[absolute_control_short|E]` shows just the word "Absolute" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it where the control value would stand, for example "Control: Absolute" in the realm window and the holding view.

label: Absolute crown authority
summary: The game concept Absolute Crown Authority: the highest level of crown authority (the law for how much power a ruler has over their vassals).
details: In a text, `[absolute_crown_authority|E]` shows "Absolute Crown Authority" linked to the concept's explanation. Vassals have -30 opinion of their liege; on top of the lower levels' effects the ruler can pick a designated heir for prestige, and vassals cannot declare any war, even on foreign rulers. Vanilla uses it in the realm window to say who may designate an heir.

label: Absolute
summary: The game concept Absolute (nomadic): the second-highest level of nomadic authority.
details: In a text, `[absolute_nomadic|E]` shows the word "Absolute" linked to the concept's explanation. At this level a migration can target de jure empire titles inside the Great Steppe, and independent rulers can settle outside the steppe with a decision. Vanilla uses it when listing the nomadic authority levels.

label: Absolute tribal authority
summary: Another name of the game concept Absolute Tribal Authority: the highest level of tribal authority (the tribal law for a ruler's power over their vassals).
details: In a text, `[absolute_tribal|E]` shows the word "Absolute" linked to the concept's explanation. Vassals have -30 opinion of their liege, and rulers can settle and become feudal. Unreformed tribal pagan rulers need this level to reform their faith. Vanilla uses it when listing the tribal authority levels.

label: Absolute tribal authority
summary: The game concept Absolute Tribal Authority: the highest level of tribal authority (the tribal law for a ruler's power over their vassals).
details: In a text, `[absolute_tribal_authority|E]` shows "Absolute Tribal Authority" linked to the concept's explanation. Vassals have -30 opinion of their liege, rulers can settle and become feudal, and unreformed tribal pagan rulers need it to reform their faith. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Promote cultural acceptance
summary: The game concept Promote Cultural Acceptance: a council task of the steward that raises the acceptance between a chosen culture and the ruler's own culture.
details: In a text, `[accept_culture|E]` shows the task's name, "Promote Cultural Acceptance", linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in perk and court texts that make the task more effective.

label: Accolade
summary: Another name of the game concept Accolade: an honor a liege gives to one of their knights, who then becomes an acclaimed knight.
details: In a text, `[acclaimed|E]` shows the word "Acclaimed" linked to the explanation of accolades. Vanilla uses it in sentences like "can be acclaimed as …" for the accolade attributes a knight qualifies for.

label: Acclaimed knight
summary: The game concept Acclaimed Knight: the knight who holds an accolade.
details: In a text, `[acclaimed_knight|E]` shows "Acclaimed Knight" linked to the concept's explanation. To qualify, a knight must be unlanded or a baron, have enough prowess, and fit an accolade attribute that none of the liege's other acclaimed knights has. Acclaimed knights are less likely to die or be captured in battle and earn glory mainly by fighting.

label: Acclaimed knight
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Acclaimed Knight (the knight who holds an accolade).
details: In a text, `[acclaimed_knight_possessive|E]` shows "Acclaimed Knight's" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in accolade texts such as "the Acclaimed Knight's opinion" or "the Acclaimed Knight's diplomacy skill".

label: Acclaimed knight
summary: The plural form of the game concept Acclaimed Knight (the knight who holds an accolade).
details: In a text, `[acclaimed_knights|E]` shows "Acclaimed Knights" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in concept, war and important-action texts.

label: Accolade
summary: The game concept Accolade: an honor a liege gives to one of their knights, who then becomes an acclaimed knight.
details: In a text, `[accolade|E]` shows "Accolade" linked to the concept's explanation. As the knight gains glory, the accolade gains ranks that unlock more and stronger attributes, and its squires aptitude improves. When the acclaimed knight dies, a successor takes over the accolade at once.

label: Accolade
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Accolade (an honor a liege gives to one of their knights).
details: In a text, `[accolade_possessive|E]` shows "Accolade's" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in phrases like "an Accolade's Glory" and "your new Accolade's Acclaimed Knight".

label: Accolade rank
summary: The game concept Accolade Rank: one of the 6 ranks an accolade climbs, each letting its owner unlock or improve accolade attribute bonuses.
details: In a text, `[accolade_rank|E]` shows "Accolade Rank" linked to the concept's explanation. Gaining glory unlocks ranks and losing glory can take them away; a lost rank disables one level of an attribute until the rank is regained.

label: Accolade rank
summary: A short name of the game concept Accolade Rank (the 6 ranks an accolade climbs with glory).
details: In a text, `[accolade_rank_short|E]` shows just the word "Rank" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it before a number, as in "Rank 3" and "Next Rank" in the accolade window.

label: Accolade rank
summary: The plural form of the game concept Accolade Rank (the 6 ranks an accolade climbs with glory).
details: In a text, `[accolade_ranks|E]` shows "Accolade Ranks" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it for example in "Reached Max Accolade Ranks".

label: Squires
summary: Another name of the game concept Squires: an accolade's squires aptitude, which shapes the traits and skills of its next acclaimed knight.
details: In a text, `[accolade_squire|E]` shows the word "Squire" linked to the concept's explanation. The aptitude has 5 levels, from Accomplished down to Pathetic, and mainly affects prowess, martial and tourney experience of the successor. Vanilla uses it for a young character trained under an acclaimed knight.

label: Squires
summary: The game concept Squires: an accolade's squires aptitude, which shapes the traits and skills of its next acclaimed knight.
details: In a text, `[accolade_squires|E]` shows "Squires" linked to the concept's explanation. There are 5 aptitude levels (Accomplished, Capable, Inexperienced, Feckless, Pathetic); the aptitude rises as the acclaimed knight gains glory and mostly improves the successor's prowess, martial and tourney experience.

label: Accolade succession
summary: The game concept Accolade Succession: what happens when an accolade's acclaimed knight dies or becomes invalid, and someone else takes over the accolade.
details: In a text, `[accolade_succession|E]` shows "Accolade Succession" linked to the concept's explanation. The replacement comes at once: first young courtiers and knights trained as the accolade's squires, then other knights, other courtiers, wanderers, and last a newly created character. The squires aptitude raises the new knight's skills.

label: Accolade attribute
summary: The game concept Accolade Attribute: one of up to 3 attributes of an accolade, each giving bonuses that grow over 3 levels.
details: In a text, `[accolade_type|E]` shows "Accolade Attribute" linked to the concept's explanation. When the accolade gains a rank, its owner can raise an attribute's level or add a new one, but the acclaimed knight must meet the new attribute's requirements (traits, skills and more).

label: Accolade attribute
summary: The plural form of the game concept Accolade Attribute (the up to 3 bonus-giving attributes of an accolade).
details: In a text, `[accolade_types|E]` shows "Accolade Attributes" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it for example in "Available Accolade Attributes:" when creating an accolade.

label: Accolade
summary: The plural form of the game concept Accolade (an honor a liege gives to one of their knights).
details: In a text, `[accolades|E]` shows "Accolades" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in important-action and accolade texts, such as being below the maximum number of accolades.

label: Activity
summary: The plural form of the game concept Activity (a special occasion a host holds for a purpose, such as a hunt).
details: In a text, `[activities|E]` shows "Activities" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it often, for example in the AI personality texts about hosting activities.

label: Activity
summary: The game concept Activity: a special occasion held for a purpose, such as a hunt to relieve stress.
details: In a text, `[activity|E]` shows "Activity" linked to the concept's explanation. The host holds it at a chosen location, which affects it, and everyone who attends must travel there. Each attendee sets an intent that they pursue during the activity.

label: Activity guest
summary: Another name of the game concept Activity Guest: any character the host invited to an activity.
details: In a text, `[activity_attending|E]` shows the word "Attending" linked to the explanation of activity guests. Vanilla uses it in coronation texts such as "Every Attending foreign ruler …".

label: Activity guest
summary: The game concept Activity Guest: any character the host invited to an activity.
details: In a text, `[activity_guest|E]` shows "Activity Guest" linked to the concept's explanation. Guests usually have less say over the activity than the host, but they still pursue their own intent.

label: Activity guest
summary: A short name of the game concept Activity Guest (a character invited to an activity).
details: In a text, `[activity_guest_short|E]` shows just the word "Guest" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in list texts like "Every Guest".

label: Activity guest
summary: The plural form of the game concept Activity Guest (the characters invited to an activity).
details: In a text, `[activity_guests|E]` shows "Activity Guests" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in coronation option texts, for example guests being more likely to join.

label: Activity guest
summary: A short plural name of the game concept Activity Guest (the characters invited to an activity).
details: In a text, `[activity_guests_short|E]` shows just the word "Guests" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the host's concept text ("which Guests to invite").

label: Activity host
summary: The game concept Activity Host: the ruler who started an activity.
details: In a text, `[activity_host|E]` shows "Activity Host" linked to the concept's explanation. The host chooses the activity type, the location, the options and which guests to invite.

label: Activity host
summary: The possessive form of the game concept Activity Host (the ruler who started an activity).
details: In a text, `[activity_host_possessive|E]` shows "Activity Host's" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in event options that are available because of the host's intent.

label: Activity host
summary: A short name of the game concept Activity Host (the ruler who started an activity).
details: In a text, `[activity_host_short|E]` shows just the word "Host" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the activity concept text.

label: Activity option
summary: The game concept Activity Option: a choice that customizes how an activity is planned.
details: In a text, `[activity_option|E]` shows "Activity Option" linked to the concept's explanation. Every activity has options, and they come with their own costs and requirements.

label: Activity option
summary: The plural form of the game concept Activity Option (the choices that customize how an activity is planned).
details: In a text, `[activity_options|E]` shows "Activity Options" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it for example in a perk text that lowers the options' cost.

label: Activity phase
summary: The game concept Activity Phase: one action stage of an activity during which its events happen, such as a contest in a tournament, a stop on a tour or a pilgrimage's destination.
details: In a text, `[activity_phase|E]` shows "Activity Phase" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it for example in the effect text for skipping the current phase.

label: Activity phase action
summary: The game concept Activity Phase Action: the chance, every 7 days during an activity, that something happens outside the regular events.
details: In a text, `[activity_phase_action|E]` shows "Activity Phase Action" linked to the concept's explanation. Such happenings appear in the top-right corner of the activity window, and what can happen depends on the activity type (for example the host gaining prestige at a feast). Sometimes nothing happens.

label: Activity phase
summary: The plural form of the game concept Activity Phase (the action stages of an activity during which events happen).
details: In a text, `[activity_phases|E]` shows "Activity Phases" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the grand activity concept text, which may have several phases.

label: Active
summary: The game concept Active: the state of an activity once the host and guests have arrived and are taking part in it.
details: In a text, `[activity_state_active|E]` shows the word "Active" linked to the concept's explanation. Its counterpart is the passive state (`[activity_state_passive|E]`).

label: Passive
summary: The game concept Passive: the state of an activity while the host or guests have not all arrived yet, or while a tour is between two stops.
details: In a text, `[activity_state_passive|E]` shows the word "Passive" linked to the concept's explanation. Its counterpart is the active state (`[activity_state_active|E]`). No vanilla text links it.

label: Activity type
summary: The game concept Activity Type: a special variant of an activity or grand activity that can be chosen when planning it.
details: In a text, `[activity_type|E]` shows "Activity Type" linked to the concept's explanation. For example, a hunt can be Standard, Falconry or Legendary when the requirements for that type are met.

label: Activity type
summary: The plural form of the game concept Activity Type (the special variants an activity can be planned as).
details: In a text, `[activity_types|E]` shows "Activity Types" linked to the concept's explanation. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Governorship confirmation
summary: The game concept Governorship Confirmation: a decision through which a governor has their appointment formally and publicly confirmed by their liege.
details: In a text, `[admin_confirmation|E]` shows the decision's name, "Governorship Confirmation", linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the decision's tooltip about attending the liege's confirmation ceremony.

label: Administrative

details: In a text, `[administrative|E]` shows "Administrative" linked to the concept's explanation. Administrative characters use influence, and some have a family estate of their own.

label: Administrative

details: In a text, `[administrative_government|E]` shows "Administrative Government" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it for example in the state rite concept text.

label: Administrative
summary: The icon form of the game concept Administrative (the bureaucratic government that appoints governors).
details: In a text, `[administrative_i|E]` shows the administrative government icon instead of a word, linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in government custom localization.

label: Adoption
summary: The game concept Adoption: bringing another character into your house and dynasty.
details: In a text, `[adoption|E]` shows "Adoption" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it in the game rule text about what unlocks adoption.

summary: Another name of the game concept Adoption: bringing another character into your house and dynasty.
details: In a text, `[adopts|E]` shows the word "Adopts" linked to the explanation of adoption. No vanilla text links it by this name.

label: Adult
summary: The game concept Adult: a character who is at least 16 years old.
details: In a text, `[adult|E]` shows "Adult" linked to the concept's explanation.

label: Adult health
summary: The game concept Adult Health: an extra health penalty that some traits, such as Ill, give only to adults.
details: In a text, `[adult_health|E]` shows "Adult Health" linked to the concept's explanation. An adult health penalty comes on top of the regular health penalty, even when both come from the same trait. Vanilla uses it as the name of the adult health modifier.

label: Adult
summary: Another name of the game concept Adult: a character who is at least 16 years old.
details: In a text, `[adulthood|E]` shows the word "Adulthood" linked to the explanation of adults. Vanilla uses it for example in the education trait text ("Upon reaching adulthood …").

label: Adult
summary: The plural form of the game concept Adult (characters who are at least 16 years old).
details: In a text, `[adults|E]` shows "Adults" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it for example in the adult health concept text.

label: Advanced succession
summary: The game concept Advanced Succession: a way of picking a title's next holder that replaces ordinary inheritance, such as naming one heir, acclamation or appointment.
details: In a text, `[advanced_succession|E]` shows "Advanced Succession" linked to the concept's explanation. Vanilla uses it next to elective succession, for example in the demand church succession interaction.

label: Battle advantage
summary: Another name of the game concept Battle Advantage: the edge that makes one side in a battle deal more damage.
details: In a text, `[advantage|E]` shows the word "Advantage" linked to the explanation of battle advantage. The higher the advantage, the more damage that side's soldiers do. A battle often starts with one side ahead because of terrain and the commander's martial skill and traits, and commander rolls can add more.

label: Battle roll
summary: Another name of the game concept Battle Roll: the random roll each commander makes during a battle to gain advantage.
details: In a text, `[advantage_roll|E]` shows "Advantage Roll" linked to the explanation of battle rolls. The rolls go from 0 to 10, are fully random, and can decide the battle. No vanilla text links it by this name.
